question: I lost my MFA factor. What should I do?
answer: According to [NL-05:S2], if a second authentication factor is lost, you should contact the Service Desk by telephone. IT Operations will reset the factor after identity verification.

sources.title: Passwords and MFA
sources.heading: Lost authentication factor
sources.text: If a second authentication factor is lost, contact the Service Desk by telephone. IT Operations resets the factor after identity verification. Never disclose an MFA code, even to someone claiming to work for IT.

sources.title: Passwords and MFA
sources.heading: Sign-in
sources.text: Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for the central company account. Passwords must contain at least 14 characters and must not be reused for personal services. Credentials are stored in the approved password manager.

sources.title: Onboarding Process
sources.heading: First week
sources.text: On the first working day, identity is verified and multi-factor authentication is configured. Security induction must be completed within the first five working days. Additional application permissions require the process in document NL-04.

sources.title: Security Incidents
sources.heading: Reporting
sources.text: Suspicious sign-ins, lost company devices and confidential data accidentally shared externally must be reported to Security immediately by telephone. Do not wait for the next team meeting. Record the time and observed facts.

sources.title: Knowledge Platform Backup Plan
sources.heading: Retention
sources.text: Backups of the internal knowledge platform are retained for 60 calendar days. Security reviews the plan annually. This retention statement does not concern Atlas customer data.
